status_meaning.complete: the group's required_output is produced by a tested path, with no known gap
status_meaning.partial: some extraction exists and is tested, but the group's required_output is not fully produced
status_meaning.custody_only: the original bytes are preserved and retrievable byte-identically, and nothing parses or converts them

custody_note: custody is universal in vNext: any bytes can be imported as a content-addressed source and survive an archive export/restore byte-identically (crates/archeaxis-archive/tests/raw_recovery.rs, and for a whole vault crates/archeaxis-archive/tests/obsidian_vault_roundtrip.rs). A custody_only row therefore states that preservation works and that parsing does not exist yet - it never claims conversion.
requirement_note: release_scope, formats and required_output are carried verbatim from the 2026-09-07 record and are re-checked against it, so the requirement cannot be quietly redefined to match what was built.

formats.implemented_now: the text route extracts the text and reports canonical line anchors, and the media type is now derived from the source name, so markdown, CSV, TSV, JSON and XML are dispatched as what they are. A `.py` source is named `text/x-python` and its declared symbols - classes, functions, async functions and imports with the line each appears on - are reported from the interpreter's own parser over the file's bytes. The route also reports the structure it can really derive in loss_receipt.params.format: markdown headings with line numbers, wiki-link, embed, markdown-link, code-fence and list counts; CSV/TSV delimiter, rows, columns, header and ragged rows; JSON parse result with top-level type, key count and nested depth; XML parse result with root, element count and depth. A document that does not parse is still projected as text and the fact says parsed false with the reason, and the reason is added to the loss list
formats.gap: there is no local-model annotation, no table or formula structure, and the symbol parser covers Python only - another source language is still projected as text without symbols. A file that does not parse reports parsed false and claims no symbols. The format facts describe the document, they are not a second addressing scheme, so anchors remain line based

formats.required_output: 快照、正文、链接、抓取时间、段落锚点
formats.implemented_now: a saved HTML snapshot reaches its own route (`html.structure`) through a worker that existed since an earlier slice with no route pointing at it. It reports the page title, the body blocks as the projection and as block anchors, and the link list with href and visible text; scripts and styles are never executed and never projected (a test asserts a script body does not appear in the stored text). The transport keeps the worker's block anchors and link list as facts under `params.worker_structure` and `params.worker_output` while the route contract carries canonical line anchors. A file with no markup at all is refused rather than reported as an empty success. F02's capture time now has an honest source: `scripts/ingest/url_snapshot.py` fetches one public URL through the bounded snapshot worker, imports the snapshot with a `url` origin whose `received_at` is the moment the body arrived, and queues the html job the content calls for; an over-cap body is refused without writing a snapshot, and a failed fetch records an error and creates no source
formats.gap: the fetcher is a driver, not a route: a running job can still not reach the network by itself, and that is deliberate - the address policy (refuse loopback, private, link-local, reserved, multicast and unmapped-name answers, and re-check every redirect target) lives in the worker the driver calls, and a DNS name that answers differently between the check and the connection is not defeated there, so egress policy at the network layer remains the real boundary. A marked-up but genuinely empty page reports that it carries no text

formats.required_output: 页面快照、正文、分页/滚动覆盖记录
formats.implemented_now: a saved dynamic page is read by the same HTML route, so its snapshot body and links are extracted like any other page: the page's own rendered markup is what the snapshot contains, and that is what is reported
formats.gap: there is still no browser, so a page whose body only exists after scripting cannot be reached: the fetch that now exists (scripts/ingest/url_snapshot.py through services/python-workers/web/worker_webpage.py) retrieves the served bytes only, and pagination or scroll coverage still cannot be recorded because nothing scrolled. The worker stays unrouted from the Core's side by design - no capability may hold a network - and its snapshot of an unscripted page is not a rendered page

formats.required_output: 原图、OCR框、阅读顺序、图示描述
formats.implemented_now: the image.ocr route runs real Tesseract and returns recognised text with canonical line anchors; the media type is derived from the source name and must be one the route accepts, so png, jpeg, tiff, webp and bmp are all dispatched as what they are (each verified end to end through the transport to the engine); OCR regions are reported as facts in the loss receipt params, each carrying the engine's own per-word score, and the regions scoring below a named review threshold are listed separately with their boxes and scores so a human knows where to look first (the threshold is described as a review aid, never a correctness measure, and the word that would turn a score into a claim never appears in the receipt); a blank image produces no invented text. A figure description is available as its own route (`image.caption`) through a local vision model: it is probed first, a missing model is a named failure, and the description is stored as a labelled candidate with its model id and prompt version rather than as extracted content. The reading order is decided from the word boxes and reported as a fact with its reason: the route runs the engine in single-block mode, so a visual row of two columns comes back as one line and the projection interleaved the columns (measured through the engine, not assumed), and the model splits each engine line along a vertical gutter that no word box crosses, orders the columns one after the other, and moves the review regions with it. The invariant is the word multiset, because splitting a line is exactly what the engine's single-block layout got wrong, and the engine order is kept whenever the reconstruction would not account for exactly the same words.
formats.gap: the model fixes column interleaving and nothing else: a phrase the engine misread stays misread, and its within-line word order is left alone; a description is model output whose quality needs a human truth pair rather than another model call; a file whose extension the Core cannot name is refused rather than guessed at; and a wrong reading can score above the review threshold

formats.implemented_now: the pdf.extract route runs PyMuPDF, returns the text with canonical page/line anchors and coverage over lines, and reports what the engine really exposed in loss_receipt.params.structure: per-page character and engine-block counts, image references, engine text blocks with their bounding boxes and first lines, and tables the engine's own finder detects with their row and column counts. Engine chatter is captured into the receipt instead of being printed, because the stdio protocol is one JSON envelope per line. The reading order of the projected text is decided by the worker and reported as a fact with its reason: the model is one vertical gutter with text on both sides, then column by column and top to bottom, applied to the page only when that holds, and it may only REORDER - it is refused whenever its reconstruction would change which lines the page holds, and it stands down entirely when the engine text carries blank separator lines, because a line-level reconstruction would not carry them; a single-column page is returned exactly as the engine gave it, and every page records whether the model applied, how many columns it saw and why it stood down
formats.gap: the model handles one gutter, so it reads two-column pages rather than an arbitrary layout, and it stands down when a line crosses the gutter or the engine text carries blank lines; blocks are engine blocks rather than linguistic paragraphs and a table detection is a detection, not a guarantee; pages are reported as facts rather than as an addressing level in the structure

formats.implemented_now: a page with no extractable text returns genuinely empty text plus an explicit loss entry naming OCR as the next route, the pages that need OCR are named in pages_without_text with their per-page character counts, the PDF route renders those pages to PNG and declares each one with its digest and size, and the Core verifies every digest, imports each page as its own source (named so the media derivation reads it as a PNG) and enqueues one image job per page - automatically, inside the same commit that completes the PDF job, so a scanned PDF chains into a real OCR job with no manual call and its recognised text lands in the store. Enqueueing is idempotent; a tampered render, a size mismatch and a name that tries to leave the transfer area are refused with a reason and leave no queued job behind, and a chaining failure is recorded as a machine receipt naming the reason while the PDF job keeps the success it earned. Each page source is now imported with an `import` origin of `<pdf source_id>#page-N` - recorded, then verified to have landed rather than assumed - and `ocr::pages_of` answers a PDF page by page with the text its own OCR job produced, exposed as `GET /api/v1/sources/:id/pages`; a page whose OCR has not run is reported with recognised false and no text, and `received_at` stays NULL because a clock value is never invented
formats.gap: the write-back is a relation, not a merge: the page's text lives on the page source and the PDF answers through it, so the PDF's own anchors still address only its text layer and a scanned page has no addressable region inside the PDF document itself. Low-scoring regions are now listed for review with their boxes and scores (see the image row), and that list is the honest form of the requirement: the route reports where to look, and a wrong reading can still score above the threshold, so the score orders review work and never stands in for a verdict

formats.required_output: 标题、段落、表、图片、来源位置
formats.implemented_now: a DOCX reaches its own route (`office.structure`). The worker that reads it has existed since the 2026-09-05 slice but had no route pointing at it, so the capability was unreachable through the job contract; it is now wired (its own worker identity, media type and engine profile). It extracts the paragraph text (verified end to end: the paragraph text reaches the store) and returns its own structure - paragraphs, tables, a media inventory and header/footer notes - which the transport keeps as a fact under `params.worker_structure` while the route contract carries canonical line anchors over the projected text. A package the worker cannot read fails the job with no text artifact. Headings are now separated from body paragraphs by what the file declares: a paragraph carries the style it references (the style definition's display name when the document defines one), and its outline level comes from its own `w:outlineLvl`, else the level that style definition assigns, else a built-in heading style name in English or Chinese; the receipt reports `style_definitions`, `paragraph_count`, `heading_count` and the heading list. A paragraph none of those describe stays a plain paragraph with no level - no outline is inferred from text, length or capitalisation
formats.gap: the worker's own paragraph and table structure is reported as a fact rather than as an addressing level, so navigation stays on line anchors; a heading is a reported fact rather than an addressing level; formatting carried on runs rather than on the paragraph style is not read, list numbering is not reconstructed, and nothing is rendered

formats.required_output: 幻灯片、文本、备注、图表引用
formats.implemented_now: a PPTX reaches the `office.structure` route through the same worker (python-pptx 1.0.2 is available here and the worker's own probe reports it). It reads slide order, shape text, speaker notes and an image count, and its own structure is kept as a fact under `params.worker_structure` while the route contract carries line anchors over the projected text. A package whose engine is missing or unreadable fails the job rather than succeeding empty. Chart data is now read too: the worker parses the package's own chart parts with the standard library and projects each series as `Series <name>: <category>=<value>` under a `slide_chart` structure entry, so a chart contributes its numbers and its own anchor instead of only being counted; the values are the file's cached results (declared as `chart_data_source` in the receipt) and a series whose data lives only in a linked workbook is reported as carrying no cached values rather than filled in
formats.gap: slide and shape structure is a reported fact rather than an addressing level, and nothing is rendered; chart numbers are the cached ones the file carries, so a chart fed by a live spreadsheet reports no values until that workbook is resolved

formats.implemented_now: an XLSX reaches the `office.structure` route through the same worker (openpyxl 3.1.5 is available here and the worker's own probe reports it). It reads sheets and cells, the formula text with the cached-value policy it states, and merged ranges, with macros never executed; its own structure is kept as a fact under `params.worker_structure` while the route contract carries line anchors. A workbook the engine cannot read fails the job rather than succeeding empty
formats.gap: sheet and cell structure is a reported fact rather than an addressing level, formula results are not calculated (only the cached value the file carries), and nothing is rendered

formats.required_output: 转写、片段/词时间、音轨、质量标记
formats.implemented_now: a real recording reaches a transcription route rather than only a header probe: `attempts.rs` declares kind `transcribe` -> capability `media.transcribe` (declared input type `audio/wav`) with worker `services/python-workers/media/worker_transcribe.py`, and the Core binds a transcript job's loss report to that capability. The projection is a transcript with time-coded cues. Long audio is split into windows by `media/window_plan.py` + `media/window_transcribe.py` under the single-sourced policy in `config/defaults.yaml` (ceiling/overhead/realtime factor), and a job carries the split as its one extra input, keyed so a resume continues instead of restarting. Word-level timing now rides the same channel: the request body may set `words`, that choice is part of the request identity so a segment-only receipt can never be replayed as an answer to a word request, and the worker reports `word_timings_requested` beside `word_timings_produced` so a request the model could not satisfy stays visible instead of reading as met. WAV/MP3/M4A/FLAC/OGG/OPUS are named container types precisely so a real recording reaches this route (attempts.rs:221-231); they stay outside `media.probe`'s accepted types, so the probe still refuses a format it cannot read.
formats.gap: segment-level cue timing is the default and word-level timing is available on request, but the group is not complete: there is still no speaker separation, and no interface asks for word timings yet (the choice exists at the HTTP boundary only). Coverage is bounded rather than total: a recording longer than the per-window budget stops at the first unreachable window and the remainder is reported `not_attempted` rather than transcribed, so a long file is partially transcribed by design and the receipt says so.

formats.required_output: 对齐的音轨、字幕、画面事件、采样覆盖
formats.implemented_now: MP4, MOV, MKV and WebM reach a video route, not only a header probe: `media.video` accepts video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/x-matroska and video/webm (attempts.rs:126-133) with worker `services/python-workers/media/worker_video.py`. That worker decodes what the probe could only describe -- it extracts a 16 kHz mono WAV of the audio track for the ASR lane and sampled keyframes as JPEGs carrying their media-time offsets, with `--frame-interval-ms` and `--max-frames` bounding the sample. The product job also transcribes the extracted audio and describes up to three sampled frames through the local vision adapter. Subtitle extraction is its own route rather than a gap: `subtitles.structure` accepts application/x-subrip and text/vtt (attempts.rs:156) with worker `document/worker_subtitles.py`, returning cue anchors that carry `offset_ms` and `duration_ms`. A truncated box or an unparseable subtitle fails or is reported rather than guessed. The limited header probe (`media.probe`) still refuses a format it cannot read.
formats.gap: coverage is by sampling and bounded, so the group is not complete on the required output: keyframes are sampled at an interval (default 10 s, at most 24) rather than reported as exhaustive frame events, and the product job describes at most three frames through the vision adapter. Nothing here separates speakers, and a video the decoder cannot open is still a named failure rather than a partial read.

formats.implemented_now: a .canvas reaches its own route (`canvas.structure`) and the worker behind it existed in this repository since the 2026-09-05 slice with no route pointing at it. It validates the canvas (an edge naming an unknown node is refused), projects the text nodes and returns node anchors that carry the node ids, plus the edges and the file/link references; the transport keeps that structure and those edges as facts under `params.worker_structure` and `params.worker_output` while the route contract carries canonical line anchors. SRT and VTT likewise have their own route (`subtitles.structure`) and their own media types (application/x-subrip, text/vtt), so a subtitle is no longer declared as plain text: the worker parses the cues and returns cue anchors that carry `offset_ms` and `duration_ms`. A subtitle file the worker cannot parse fails the job. Each canvas node also comes back with the geometry the file declares - `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, numbers only, a string or null coordinate is dropped rather than coerced - plus its `color` and `style` when they are non-blank strings, and every edge is preserved verbatim so an edge's sides and endpoint ports travel with it
formats.gap: the node and cue anchors are kept as facts rather than as an addressing level in the projection, a declared colour is reported as the string the file holds, not resolved to a rendered swatch, and z-order, tabs and group containment are not computed, and the text route's JSON reading of a canvas remains available without being the structure path

formats.required_output: 章节/邮件头/附件引用及结构
formats.implemented_now: a saved mail message (.eml) is resolved as the text it is and the route reports its RFC 822 structure as facts: the recognised headers (from, to, cc, subject, date, message-id), how many headers were found, the MIME part count, whether a text and an HTML body exist, and the attachments by name and size. An attachment is now also extracted: with a transfer area from the Core, the worker writes each attachment under a flat safe name and declares it the way a container does - name, file, bytes, sha256 - so the Core verifies every digest and size, imports each attachment as its own source recording `<mail source>#<attachment name>`, and queues the route the attachment's own name selects; an attachment no route can read stays a custody-only source instead of disappearing. The mail itself is still projected verbatim, so the raw file stays the source of record. Detection is reported as a detection ('RFC 822 header shape, not by media type'), and a file that merely begins with 'From:' is not called a message. EPUB chapters were already read from the spine. ODT, ODS, ODP and RTF now have a reader in this path too: an ODF package is opened by its own content.xml (after its mimetype entry is checked against the media type the name claims), giving headings with their outline level, paragraphs, sheet cells carrying the file's own stored value, presentation pages, and a named cap when a row or column declares a repetition larger than 512; RTF is projected with its control words stripped by the declared engine. Each is anchored, and a package that lies about what it is, has no readable text or contains an unsafe member is refused rather than projected as an empty success
formats.gap: attachment extraction is one level deep - an attachment that is itself a container is imported but not expanded - and a mail whose only parts are attachments fails the job rather than succeeding with an empty projection, because there is no body to anchor; the binary .msg container stays out of reach until a reader for it exists; ODF headings, cells and pages are reported facts rather than a navigation level, and ODF styles, fields, embedded objects and hyperlink targets are not followed; RTF tables, footnotes and styles are not reconstructed

formats.implemented_now: the original file is preserved as bytes, which is the part of the requirement that must never be lost. `.xls` now has a reader - the declared xlrd engine - so it reaches `office.structure` by name instead of being refused: each sheet is projected with its cells typed as text, number, date, boolean, error or empty, a date is converted with the workbook's own datemode, and every sheet additionally comes out as a converted CSV written to the Core-owned transfer area and declared by digest the way a container declares members, so the Core verifies each one, imports it as its own source recording `<workbook source>#<sheet>.csv` and queues the text route for it. The loss report names what the conversion cannot carry: formulas are not recalculated (only the value the file caches), and number formats, styles, merged-cell spans, charts, images, pivots and macros do not cross into the CSV
formats.gap: only `.xls` of the three legacy binary families has a reader here - `.doc` and `.ppt` stay unnamed and custody-only because no engine for them exists in this repository; the committed fixture is project-authored (written once with `xlwt` as an authoring tool, which is not a declared dependency), so no Excel-authored document has been verified and FMT-21 per-extension real-sample acceptance stays NOT_RUN; the CSV counterpart is a value-level conversion, not a rendered or formatted one

formats.required_output: 容器到文件到知识的来源关系
formats.implemented_now: a container has its own route (`archive.inventory`), because a ZIP is binary and decoding it as text would produce noise. The worker reads the container's own directory, projects an inventory listing - one member per line, name and size - with canonical line anchors, and reports the member, file and directory counts, the uncompressed and compressed totals, the compression methods present, nested containers and encrypted members. It also extracts the readable members into the transfer area and declares each one with its digest; the Core verifies every digest and size, imports each member as its own source, records where it came from as an origin (`import` with `<container source_id>#<member path>`, and verifies the relation really landed), and enqueues a job for each member whose name resolves to a route. A member no route can read is kept as a source and reported as custody-only. `GET /api/v1/sources/:id/members` then answers what is inside a container and which parts were read, with `readable` meaning a transform exists rather than that the content was understood, and a note saying the list is what was imported rather than the container's whole inventory. The host panel shows that list too, marking the members that were kept but not read, and it distinguishes an unknown container (the Core's 404) from an empty one instead of drawing an empty table. The receipt states that the projection is an inventory of the container and NOT the members' contents; a corrupt container, an empty container and a member that does not match its declaration are all refused A FOLDER now has an ingestion path too: scripts/ingest/directory_batch.py walks a directory, imports each file as its own source through the Core's HTTP API, enqueues the job the file's kind calls for, and appends one JSONL line per attempt. It resumes on the latest attempt that actually did something (a skip record can never be the last word, or a third run would redo the whole folder), and it reports every exclusion rather than dropping a path silently. A file whose extension the driver maps to no kind is still imported and recorded as carrying no job, with the reason: measured against a real Core, the Core ACCEPTS the import of a file whose extension it cannot name, so the refusal that matters happens at route resolution, and the driver names the missing job instead of guessing one.
formats.gap: the folder driver is a script that speaks HTTP, not a Core route or a UI affordance, so a folder is ingested by running it rather than by asking the product; the member relation is recorded as an origin reference rather than as a first-class container-to-file edge, so a container's parts cannot be addressed; members beyond the extraction caps are not expanded; a member that has been read is still not promoted to knowledge; and files the driver has no kind for are imported but left without a job

formats.required_output: 原生文件与派生预览、转换覆盖说明
formats.implemented_now: the native file is imported and preserved byte-identically; the boundary is deliberate rather than accidental
formats.gap: no derived preview and no conversion is attempted, so conversion coverage is stated as zero rather than implied - the requirement is that the original must not be lost to an impossible conversion, and that part holds
